archetypes.name: doc-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan corrects the same factual claim across five doc files; this reviewer checks whether each planned replacement is semantically accurate against the actual cleanup.sh code and whether the plan omits any additional sites with the same stale description.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan claims five documentation files (cleanup.md, test-cleanup.md, SECURITY.md, docs/configuration-and-permissions.md, skills/cleanup/SKILL.md) contain inaccurate retention-logic descriptions and proposes specific replacement text for each. For every planned doc edit, verify the proposed replacement accurately reflects what cleanup.sh actually does — cache-pass enumeration strategy, maxdepth-5 nested scan, fail-safe skip-on-error. Check that the corrected sites use consistent terminology and semantics with one another; a correction accurate for SECURITY.md but subtly inconsistent with cleanup.md is a plan defect. Also check whether any other files in the scope list or skill directory describe the same retention behavior and would remain inconsistent if the plan is executed as written. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stub-design
archetypes.rationale: The sole real code deliverable is a new test case whose correctness depends entirely on the stub injection design; this reviewer checks whether the adjacent-pair detection, PATH_PREFIX mechanism, and assertion set are mechanically sound.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan proposes a find stub injected via PATH_PREFIX that exits 2 when its argument list contains the adjacent pair -maxdepth 5, delegating all other calls to /usr/bin/find. Verify that the adjacent-pair detection condition is sufficient to distinguish the nested-activity scan from the three other find call sites in cleanup.sh (cache enumeration, /tmp pass, symlink reap) without false positives that would break cache enumeration or false negatives that would leave the fail-safe untested. Verify the PATH_PREFIX injection pattern is used consistently with existing harness stubs (e.g., write_stub_pgrep) and that /usr/bin/find is the correct absolute path on the CI platform. Check whether the four planned assertions — exit 0, warning string 'failed to scan session activity', stale dir still present, CACHE_REMOVED=0 — are reliable and complete, specifically whether the warning string matches what larch_err actually emits in the fail-safe branch of should_remove_by_age. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
